verdict.rationale: BigQuery's pricing page documents two compute pricing models: on-demand billing per TiB processed with 1 TiB free each month, and capacity billing in slots over time. Community users confirm the console shows bytes to be scanned before a query runs, so on-demand cost per query is 'comprehensible' at $6.25/TB. However, other users report that the bytes-scanned and slots abstraction makes costs hard to anticipate, citing a $14k surprise bill from a script. Missing for 10: first-party published unit rates and storage pricing detail in the evidence, a documented pricing calculator or monthly-estimation guidance, and clear guidance for predicting slot/capacity spend.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, the pricing model is documented clearly enough that I can estimate a monthly bill for my workload before committing

citations.quote: With this pricing model, you are charged for the number of bytes processed by each query. The first 1 TiB of query data processed per month is free.
BigQuery offers a choice of two compute pricing models for running queries
you are charged for compute capacity used to run queries, measured in slots (virtual CPUs) over time
Store 10 GiB of data and run up to 1 TiB of queries for free per month.
